text.en: My name is Bela. I have two brothers, Banku Bhaiya and little Bishu, and we love to play chhupan-chhupai (hide and seek) outside our house. My family, my friends and our dog Shiru fill my days with games, songs, food and work. Come and see how a family lives, plays, helps and cares.

Bela lives with her parents, her brothers Banku and Bishu, and her grandparents. Together they are one family. The children play chhupan-chhupai, hide and seek, in the open space outside their house. They also play peek-a-boo with little Bishu, hiding and suddenly showing their face and saying peek-a-boo. They have planted a garden with many flowering plants. Relatives, friends and neighbours come to the garden, sit, talk, share jokes and laugh together. Sometimes their father and mother, tired after a hard day's work, also sit and relax in the garden, so the whole family enjoys spending the evening together.
On rainy days the family sits under a small shelter in the garden. It is great fun to sit outside when it rains. They play games such as antakshari and snakes and ladders. Bela's mother and Dadiji, her grandmother, make hot pakodas and tea, and everybody, grandparents too, enjoys them together. Dadiji sings songs about the rain and teaches them to the children, so they join in the singing. Songs are passed from grandparents to grandchildren in this way. We can sing a rain song in class with our friends, and we can also write down the names of our own family members, how they are related to us and what we call them, like Mausi for the mother's sister.
Bela's grandfather, Dadaji, taught Banku and Bela the games he played with his friends when he was young. He joins in their games too. Shiru, the dog, is a member of the family and has a special place in the home. He runs around, barking and wagging his tail with joy. Banku and Bela never hurt Shiru and they share their food with him. We should be kind and caring towards animals and should not tease or hurt them. We can ask our grandparents which games they played when they were small and play them with them.
Families are big and small and different, and we love them all. A family can have a few or many members. There can be parents (mother and father), grandparents like Dadiji and Dadaji, brothers and sisters like Banku and Bela, and other elders in a family. Everybody loves each other and takes care of each other. Families also love and care for animals, trees and plants. Cows, buffaloes, dogs, parrots, cats and goats can be a part of a family. We can look around our neighbourhood and see many types of families, so we must not say that only one kind of family is right.
In our homes we do many things together. Bela's Dadiji oils her hair and braids it every morning before school, humming a song, and this makes Bela happy. Bela's parents help each other in all the housework, from cooking and cleaning to shopping for groceries. Dadaji loves gardening, and Bela helps him in the garden. Banku helps in cleaning and chopping vegetables. Everyone in the family does some work and everyone helps. Some people in the family, like grandparents, small children or someone who is sick, need special care and support, and we should help them.
Munni is one of Bela's closest friends. Munni and her mother, Kusum Mausi, live near her house. Kusum Mausi is the mother's close friend, who is like a sister. Kusum Mausi is an excellent cook and makes sweets and special dishes during festivals. She and Munni join the family in all festivals. Munni is very good at making rangoli, using colours from dried flowers, leaves and flowers. Bela loves to help her. We learn many things from our family members and neighbours, and we can teach them things too.
Our family also includes relatives who may not live with us. They are related to us through our parents, our mother or father. A relative can be an uncle like Mohan Chacha, who is father's brother, or an aunt like a Mausi, who is mother's sister. Their names for us and our names for them show how we are related. We can make a table of who does which work in our home: cooking food, watering plants, mending things, cleaning the house and buying things from the market. When we share the work, the home runs smoothly and everyone has time to play, rest and be together.
On a holiday Bela went to the park with Dadaji. Their friends Niku, Rinki, Rohit, Ronnie and Tara were playing pitthoo, a game with a pile of stones and a ball. They made two teams. Dadaji hit the stones with the ball and scattered them, and they ran to pile the stones up fast while the others tried to hit them with the ball. After some time they were tired, so Dadaji asked them to rest. Then he bought them ice cream and they went home as it grew dark, after a lot of fun playing, laughing and eating together. Playing with friends and elders keeps us happy and healthy, and good games teach us to take turns and work in a team.

problem.en: Make a table to show how our relatives are related to us.

text.en: Write the name of the relative, for example Urmila.

why.en: The first column names the person.

text.en: Write how she is related to you, such as mother's sister.

why.en: The second column shows the relationship.

text.en: Write what you call her, such as Mausi.

why.en: The third column shows how we address them with respect.

problem.en: Make a rangoli from fallen leaves and flowers.

text.en: Collect leaves and flowers that have fallen on the ground. Do not pluck flowers from plants.

why.en: We use what has already fallen so that we do not harm the plants.

text.en: Place a big flower in the middle and arrange leaves and petals around it in a pattern.

why.en: A pattern makes the rangoli look neat and pretty.

text.en: Look at your rangoli and tell a friend what you used and why it is pretty.

why.en: Making something together helps us learn from each other, as Bela learns from Munni.

prompt.en: Tell a friend how the members of a family show love and care for each other, and how we should treat a pet.

requiredIdeas.en: Family members help each other with work
They play, sing, eat and spend time together
Elders and those who need care are helped
We are kind to animals and never hurt them

commonMisconceptions.en: Only people are part of a family
We can tease a pet for fun

points.en: A family can be big or small, and everyone in it loves and cares for each other.
Family members play, sing, eat and work together.
Grandparents teach songs and games, and we learn from elders and neighbours.
Pets like Shiru can be part of the family, and we must be kind to animals.
Relatives are the people related to us through our mother or father.
Friends and neighbours share festivals, games and happy times.
